name: Kate Bush
hook: A teenage songwriter whose demo David Gilmour paid for, who took up the Fairlight sampler in 1980, and who produced her own records from 1982.
blurb: Kate Bush was born on 30 July 1958 in Bexleyheath, near London, and grew up in an old farmhouse in East Wickham. She was writing songs as a young teenager. When she was 16, David Gilmour of Pink Floyd paid for her to record a proper demo, and it got her a contract with EMI. In 1978, aged 19, her song 'Wuthering Heights' went to number one in Britain, the first time a woman reached number one there with a song she wrote entirely herself. In early 1980, singing backing vocals on Peter Gabriel's third album, she met the Fairlight, an early sampler that could play back any recorded sound from a keyboard, and used it heavily on 'Never for Ever' that year. 'The Dreaming' (1982) was the first album she produced herself, and she has produced every album since; 'Hounds of Love' (1985) reached number one in the UK. She stopped touring after 1979 and did not play live again until a run of concerts in 2014. In 2022 her 1985 song 'Running Up That Hill' was used in 'Stranger Things' and became a hit all over again, reaching number one in Britain and number three in America.

signatureTracks.title: Wuthering Heights
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Written as a teenager after a television adaptation of the novel: her first single and a UK number one.

signatureTracks.title: Babooshka
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: From 'Never for Ever', the first of her albums built with the Fairlight sampler; listen for the smashing glass.

signatureTracks.title: Running Up That Hill (A Deal with God)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Self-produced, built on a Fairlight and a drum machine, and a hit twice, 37 years apart.
